rows.content:
:::card title="The sealed satchel"
🔒
SEAL UNBROKEN
::: Marro doesn't look at the satchel. He looks at your face, then at the door behind you, then back to you. "Forty gold," he repeats, like the words are a blade he's testing. "You've got six in your pocket and a wet cloak. So. Who's the buyer, really?" He leans in, smelling of pipe smoke and old paper. "This seal isn't city mint. It's the salt-glass kind. Harbormaster's office, or his cousin's." His eyes narrow. "If the watch opens your case up tomorrow, Marro knows nothing. Agreed?" Rain hammers the shutters. Somewhere down the street, a bell tolls the hour.

rows.content:
:::card title="Ragged map on bark"
RAT ALLEY
behind the chandlery
⚠ Gessa's den — she hits hard
::: Rat Alley runs low and wet between two high walls, the kind of place a lantern is wasted. The rain here is thicker, slicking the stones until they shine like black glass. Behind the chandlery you can smell tallow and something rotting in the gutter. At a broken table by the wall sits a broad woman with a shaved left temple and a scar through her lip. One eye is a dull white socket; the other is working you like a coin. 'Courier,' she says, no greeting. 'Marro sends more of you.' She's holding something under her shawl — you'd bet it's the ledger.

rows.content:
:::card title="The Ledger — brass clasp shut"
CUSTOMS HOUSE · SALTMEERE
Ledger of Tides
Brass clasp — shut
::: The linen strip goes tight around your ribs and the breath comes shallow, but you can hold it. Rain hammers the wet boards above you. Somewhere a distant bell tolls the hour — you've got until dawn, which in Saltmere means maybe four more hours of dark. The road out of Rat Alley runs past the chandlery's loading dock. Marro's waiting room in the Drowned Lantern isn't far, but the ledger's clasp is shut tight, and you know a fence pays better for what he can read than what he has to pry open himself.

rows.content:
The fish market is a river of splashing boots. You weave between gutted mackerel and ice, ribs heaving with every stride. The watch bells clang over the harbor, and two lanterns swing ahead of you — constables, moving with the crowd rather than against it.

You duck through a gap in the stalls and out onto the quay. The Drowned Lantern's lamp burns gold against the rain, its doors ten paces down the wet flagstones.

rows.content:
The harbormaster takes the ledger with steady, grateful hands and sets it on his desk. 'By the saints, that's worth its weight in gold to me.' He slides Marro's forty gold purse across, then pauses. 'And you'll take a small escort fee? The watch will be asking questions. Say you delivered the parcel under cover of the dark.'

The job is done, but the city's eyes are now on your name.

rows.content:
The Lantern's door is still swinging when you push through, and Marro is on his feet. 'The ledger's back, so the ring's yours. And you look like hell.' He grins and pulls another small purse from beneath a crate of rope. 'Fifty for the ledger, like the harbormaster agreed. You're out.' :::card title="Settled"
LEDGER RETURNED
HARBORMASTER ILSE — PAID
MARRO — PAID
DEBT: NONE
::: The rain on the taproom windows hammers all night.
